text:
alex: 10:08 UTC — quick heads-up: EU keystore-proxy started returning 429s, kube autoscaler began draining a few GPU nodes in eu-west-1. Users seeing elevated inference latencies.
priya: which 429s? proxy-level or upstream KMS? can you paste a log line?
alex: proxy logs show `rate_limited` with header `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0`. snippet: ```json
{"level":"warn","msg":"rate_limited","client_id":"svc-platform","region":"eu-west-1"}
```
jamal: that sounds like the per-client QPS guard on the keystore-proxy. we changed `rate_limit_per_client` to 50 last week for safety.
sasha: are these decrypts from node bootstrap (kube-secret agent) or user requests? important for mitigation.
morgan: checking request identities — early look shows bursts from `kube-secret-agent` instances during node join (disk decrypts + token fetch). autoscaler warmup is amplifying the burst.
tina: security note: if we change caching or limits, make sure decrypt audit coverage stays intact. KMS decrypt events are required for compliance.
alex: ops-bot shows drains with reason `keystore-rate-limit`. example command we saw during automation: `kubectl drain gpu-node-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
ops-bot: (system) node gpu-node-23 drained by autoscaler, reason: keystore-rate-limit, ts=3642001120
jamal: short-term plan ideas: bump `rate_limit_per_client` for eu region to 200, increase keystore-proxy token cache TTL to 5m, and add detailed proxy-side decrypt logging to S3 for a window. long-term: spread decrypts during bootstrap.
priya: cost implications? more caching reduces KMS calls but more detailed logs to S3 will cost. need estimate.
morgan: rough cost: extra S3 ingestion ~$0.20/hr, if node boot storms keep happening KMS requests could be $5–15/hr; very workload-dependent.
sasha: quick fix for startup: add a randomized jitter/backoff in kube-secret-agent so decrypts per node are distributed across 30s. I can land a small client change quickly.
tina: security: I approve proxy audit sink for 24h with 7d retention. will open the approval ticket and enable. we need to tag logs with `keystore_ratelimit_incident`.
alex: rollout plan: canary patch in eu — update `keystore-proxy-config` (increase `rate_limit_per_client`), restart 2 pods in canary, monitor for 15m, then roll. I'll do the canary at ~10:20 UTC.
jamal: also ensure `keystore-proxy` emits `X-Client-ID` in logs so we can filter by client id.
priya: also add an alert if `.429_count` > 5/min sustained across region for 10m.
ops-bot: (system) alert created: keystore.429.euwest1 threshold=5/min, notify=@oncall @eng-platform
morgan: I'll watch billing and the alert dashboard. will post a cost estimate if we see sustained activity.
alex: canary rolled, 2 pods restarted, no new drains in last 5m. monitoring continues.
sasha: I'll land kube-secret-agent backoff PR to staging now; will test bootstrap behavior.
tina: audit sink enabled, initial logs flowing to `s3://redwood-keystore-incident/eu/3642001111/`. retention set to 7d.
priya: sounds good. if stable after 30m we keep changes. if not, revert and investigate further.
morgan: note: we should follow up with infra-runbook entry: "keystore proxy rate-limit incident — node bootstrap mitigation" so oncall has playbook. I'll create the doc.
alex: summary + assignments: alex -> keystore rate-limit canary roll (done); sasha -> kube-secret-agent backoff PR; tina -> proxy audit S3 sink (done); morgan -> billing + runbook; priya -> alert tuning. check-in in 1h. thanks team :thumbsup:
